claims.text: AWS evaluates the applicable policies to decide whether to allow or deny a request.

anchor.quote: AWS evaluates the policies that apply and decides whether to allow or deny it

claims.text: Every request is denied by default.

anchor.quote: By default, every request is denied.

claims.text: The default denial is called an implicit deny.

anchor.quote: This is called an implicit deny.

claims.text: The account root user has full access by default.

anchor.quote: The account root user is the exception, because it has full access by default.

claims.text: AWS first checks all applicable policies for an explicit deny.

anchor.quote: AWS first checks all applicable policies for an explicit deny.

claims.text: An explicit deny in any policy makes the final decision deny, even if another policy allows the request.

anchor.quote: the final decision is deny, even when another policy allows it

claims.text: If there is no explicit deny, AWS looks for an allow.

anchor.quote: If there is no explicit deny, AWS looks for an allow.

claims.text: A request is allowed only if at least one applicable policy contains an explicit allow.

anchor.quote: A request is allowed only if at least one applicable policy contains an explicit allow.

claims.text: If no policy allows the request, the implicit deny stands and the request is denied.

anchor.quote: If no policy allows the request, the implicit deny stands and the request is denied.

claims.text: Some policy types act as guardrails.

anchor.quote: Some policy types act as guardrails.

claims.text: Service control policies, permission boundaries and session policies never grant permissions by themselves.

A request must be allowed by a granting policy and must also fall inside each applicable guardrail.

anchor.quote: When one applies, the request must be allowed by a policy that grants permission, and it must also fall inside each guardrail that applies.
